details.label: Summary
details.text: A few severe storms capable of large hail and damaging winds are possible this afternoon/evening

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Towering cumulus can be seen in visible satellite imagery across northeast Ohio and far northwest Pennsylvania this afternoon within a region of 2500 J/kg MLCAPE and 40 to 45 knots of effective shear (per SPC HRRR-based mesoanalysis). The Pittsburgh 18Z RAOB showed an environment favorable for severe storms with 3100 J/kg MLCAPE and 38 knots of effective shear. Therefore, any storms which develop will likely be severe with a damaging wind/large hail threat. However, given relatively weak forcing across the region, storm coverage remains uncertain. Current cloud trends and latest HRRR/RRFS time-lagged guidance suggest scattered storm coverage, which would increase watch likelihood. However, the lack of forcing does cast some doubt on overall storm coverage. Therefore, 60% watch probabilities seem appropriate at this time, but if greater storm coverage appears likely, a watch will be needed

details.label: Most probable threats
